title: Metallurgy

notes.heading: 1. Key Ores, Gangue & Concentration Methods
notes.proseLatex: All ores are minerals, but NOT all minerals are ores (an ore allows profitable metal extraction). Must-know JELET ores: Bauxite ($\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3\cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$) and Cryolite ($\text{Na}_3\text{AlF}_6$) for $\text{Al}$; Haematite ($\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3$), Magnetite ($\text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4$), Siderite ($\text{FeCO}_3$) for $\text{Fe}$; Copper pyrites ($\text{CuFeS}_2$), Malachite ($\text{CuCO}_3\cdot\text{Cu(OH)}_2$) for $\text{Cu}$; Zinc blende ($\text{ZnS}$), Calamine ($\text{ZnCO}_3$) for $\text{Zn}$; Galena ($\text{PbS}$) for $\text{Pb}$. Sulphide ores are concentrated by FROTH FLOTATION (pine oil collector, $\text{NaCN}$ depressant for $\text{ZnS}/\text{PbS}$), while bauxite uses Bayer chemical leaching.

keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Match metal ores to formulas and concentration techniques.

notes.heading: 2. Calcination vs Roasting, Smelting, Hall-Héroult & Refining
notes.proseLatex: CALCINATION heats carbonate/hydrated ores in ABSENCE (or limited supply) of air ($\text{ZnCO}_3 \to \text{ZnO} + \text{CO}_2$), whereas ROASTING heats sulphide ores in EXCESS air ($2\text{ZnS} + 3\text{O}_2 \to 2\text{ZnO} + 2\text{SO}_2$). Blast-furnace iron smelting uses limestone ($\text{CaCO}_3 \to \text{CaO}$) as basic flux to remove acidic $\text{SiO}_2$ gangue as $\text{CaSiO}_3$ slag. Highly electropositive $\text{Al}$ is extracted electrolytically via Hall-Héroult (alumina dissolved in molten $\text{Na}_3\text{AlF}_6 + \text{CaF}_2$ to lower melting point and raise conductivity). Ultrapure refining methods: electrolytic ($\text{Cu, Zn}$), Mond process ($\text{Ni(CO)}_4$), van Arkel ($\text{Ti, Zr}$), and zone refining ($\text{Si, Ge}$).

keyFormulas.label: Slag Formation & Refining Process Map
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Distinguish calcination vs roasting, acidic vs basic flux, and named refining processes.

examples.problemLatex: Why are cryolite ($\text{Na}_3\text{AlF}_6$) and fluorspar ($\text{CaF}_2$) added to $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ in the Hall-Héroult cell?
stepsLatex: Pure $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ melts above $2300\text{ K}$ and is a poor electrical conductor.
Adding $\text{Na}_3\text{AlF}_6 + \text{CaF}_2$ lowers the fusion temperature to $\sim 1140\text{ K}$ and sharply increases melt electrical conductivity.
examples.answerLatex: Lowers fusion point and boosts electrical conductivity

notes.heading: 3. Engineering Alloys & Compositions
notes.proseLatex: High-yield JELET alloy compositions: Brass ($\text{Cu} + \text{Zn}$), Bronze ($\text{Cu} + \text{Sn}$), German silver ($\text{Cu} + \text{Zn} + \text{Ni}$ — contains $0\%$ silver!), Gunmetal ($\text{Cu} + \text{Sn} + \text{Zn}$), Solder ($\text{Pb} + \text{Sn}$), Duralumin ($\text{Al} + \text{Cu} + \text{Mg} + \text{Mn}$, aircraft frames), Stainless steel ($\text{Fe} + \text{Cr} + \text{Ni} + \text{C}$), and Nichrome ($\text{Ni} + \text{Cr} + \text{Fe}$, heating coils).

wbjeebTraps: GERMAN SILVER contains ZERO silver ($\text{Ag} = 0\%$) — it is purely $\text{Cu} + \text{Zn} + \text{Ni}$!
Copper pyrites ($\text{CuFeS}_2$) and Iron pyrites ($\text{FeS}_2$, 'fool's gold'): $\text{FeS}_2$ is rarely used for iron extraction because of high sulphur content.
Calcination = NO/limited air (carbonates/hydrates); Roasting = EXCESS air (sulphides) — never swap the two!

conceptPrimer.heading: Ore vs Mineral — and the Ore Formulas That Pay
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Every ore is a mineral, but not every mineral is an ore: an ore is the mineral from which the metal can be extracted PROFITABLY. JELET's must-know list: bauxite $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3\cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and cryolite $\text{Na}_3\text{AlF}_6$ (Al); haematite $\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3$, magnetite $\text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4$, siderite $\text{FeCO}_3$ (Fe); copper pyrites $\text{CuFeS}_2$, malachite $\text{CuCO}_3\cdot\text{Cu(OH)}_2$ (Cu); zinc blende $\text{ZnS}$, calamine $\text{ZnCO}_3$ (Zn); galena $\text{PbS}$ (Pb). Micro-check: iron pyrites $\text{FeS}_2$ (fool's gold) is NOT a workable iron ore — too much sulphur.

conceptPrimer.heading: Concentration: Match the Method to the Ore
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Gangue (unwanted rocky matrix) is stripped before extraction. Sulphide ores go to FROTH FLOTATION: powdered ore + water + pine oil (collector) — air bubbles carry sulphide particles up; $\text{NaCN}$ acts as depressant when $\text{ZnS}$ must be separated from $\text{PbS}$. Bauxite (an oxide hydrate) uses Bayer chemical LEACHING with hot concentrated NaOH. Magnetite, being ferromagnetic, uses magnetic separation. Micro-check: $\text{ZnS}$ is a sulphide $\Rightarrow$ froth flotation, never leaching.

conceptPrimer.heading: Calcination vs Roasting — and Flux + Slag
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: CALCINATION heats carbonate/hydrated ores with NO (or limited) air: $\text{ZnCO}_3 \to \text{ZnO} + \text{CO}_2$. ROASTING heats sulphide ores in EXCESS air: $2\text{ZnS} + 3\text{O}_2 \to 2\text{ZnO} + 2\text{SO}_2$. A FLUX binds the gangue chemically: $\underbrace{\text{CaO}}_{\text{basic flux}} + \underbrace{\text{SiO}_2}_{\text{acidic gangue}} \to \underbrace{\text{CaSiO}_3}_{\text{slag}}$ — limestone is the blast furnace's cleaning agent. Micro-check: carbonate + no air $=$ calcination; sulphide + excess air $=$ roasting — never swap them.

conceptPrimer.heading: Blast Furnace Iron Smelting
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Inside the blast furnace, coke burns to CO which reduces haematite, while limestone decomposes ($\text{CaCO}_3 \to \text{CaO} + \text{CO}_2$) to supply the basic flux that mops up acidic $\text{SiO}_2$ gangue as $\text{CaSiO}_3$ slag floating on the molten iron. Micro-check: the furnace sells two products — pig iron (metal) and $\text{CaSiO}_3$ slag (waste); both come from one limestone charge.

conceptPrimer.heading: Hall–Héroult: Electrolytic Aluminium
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Aluminium is too electropositive for carbon reduction, so pure alumina is dissolved in molten cryolite $\text{Na}_3\text{AlF}_6$ + fluorspar $\text{CaF}_2$: pure $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ melts above $2300\ \text{K}$, but the melt fuses near $\sim 1140\ \text{K}$ and conducts far better. At the cathode $\text{Al}^{3+} + 3e^- \to \text{Al}$; the carbon anode is consumed burning the liberated oxygen. Micro-check: cryolite's job is SOLVENT/FLUX — it lowers the fusion point and raises conductivity; it does not chemically reduce alumina.

conceptPrimer.heading: Refining Map and Engineering Alloys
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Ultrapure routes: electrolytic refining (Cu, Zn), Mond process (Ni via $\text{Ni(CO)}_4$, decomposed at $\sim 230^\circ\text{C}$ on Ni powder), van Arkel iodide method (Ti, Zr), zone refining (Si, Ge — melt zone drags impurities along). High-yield alloys: brass $\text{Cu}+\text{Zn}$, bronze $\text{Cu}+\text{Sn}$, german silver $\text{Cu}+\text{Zn}+\text{Ni}$ (ZERO silver), gunmetal $\text{Cu}+\text{Sn}+\text{Zn}$, solder $\text{Pb}+\text{Sn}$, duralumin $\text{Al}+\text{Cu}+\text{Mg}+\text{Mn}$ (aircraft), stainless steel $\text{Fe}+\text{Cr}+\text{Ni}+\text{C}$, nichrome $\text{Ni}+\text{Cr}+\text{Fe}$ (heating coils). Micro-check: the name lies — german silver contains $0\%$ Ag.

keyDefinitions.definition: Mineral: natural compound of a metal. Ore: the mineral from which extraction is PROFITABLE — every ore is a mineral, not conversely.
The unwanted earthy impurity (e.g. $\text{SiO}_2$) mixed with the ore.
Substance added to combine with gangue and form fusible slag; basic flux (CaO) for acidic gangue, acidic flux (SiO₂) for basic gangue.
Fusible flux–gangue combination ($\text{CaSiO}_3$) that floats on the metal and is skimmed off.
Concentration of sulphide ores: pine-oil-coated sulphide particles ride air bubbles; gangue sinks.
Heating carbonate/hydrated ores in absence (or limited supply) of air; volatile matter (CO₂, H₂O) leaves.
Heating sulphide ores in EXCESS air; sulphur leaves as SO₂.
Carbon/CO reduction of the roasted/calcined ore to molten metal in a furnace (blast furnace for iron).
Electrolytic extraction of Al from alumina dissolved in molten cryolite + fluorspar.
Ultrapurification (Si, Ge): a moving melt zone carries impurities to one end of the ingot.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: The ore of aluminium with formula $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3\cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is:
mcqSelfTest.explanation: Bauxite is the hydrated oxide; cryolite $\text{Na}_3\text{AlF}_6$ is an Al COMPOUND but used as electrolyte solvent, not as the extracted ore.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: Froth flotation is the concentration method of choice for:
mcqSelfTest.explanation: Sulphide particles are wetted by pine oil and float; oxides/carbonates use other routes (bauxite: leaching).

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: In froth flotation of $\text{ZnS}$–$\text{PbS}$ mixtures, $\text{NaCN}$ acts as a:
mcqSelfTest.explanation: $\text{NaCN}$ depresses (keeps down) $\text{ZnS}$ so $\text{PbS}$ floats first — a selective depressant, not the collector (that's pine oil).
Carbonate + absence of air: $\text{ZnCO}_3 \to \text{ZnO} + \text{CO}_2$. No $\text{SO}_2$ — that's the roasting fingerprint.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: The correctly balanced roasting equation for zinc blende is:
mcqSelfTest.explanation: Balance check: Zn $2=2$, S $2=2$, O $6 = 2 + 4$. The other options break the oxygen count.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: The slag formed in the blast furnace during iron smelting is:
mcqSelfTest.explanation: $\text{CaO}$ (basic flux) + $\text{SiO}_2$ (acidic gangue) $\to \text{CaSiO}_3$ slag. $\text{CaO}$ is the flux, not the slag.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: Cryolite and fluorspar are added to alumina in the Hall–Héroult cell because they:

options.latex: lower the fusion point and raise conductivity

mcqSelfTest.explanation: Pure alumina melts above $2300\ \text{K}$ and conducts poorly; the cryolite–fluorspar melt fuses near $\sim 1140\ \text{K}$ and conducts far better. Reduction happens at the CATHODE electrically.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: The Mond process is used for refining:
mcqSelfTest.explanation: Ni forms volatile $\text{Ni(CO)}_4$ which decomposes on hot Ni powder. Ti/Zr go through van Arkel iodides; Si/Ge through zone refining.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: Zone refining is the ultrapurification route for:
mcqSelfTest.explanation: Semiconductor-grade Si/Ge: a moving melt zone drags impurities along the ingot to one end.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: German silver is an alloy of:
mcqSelfTest.explanation: $\text{Cu} + \text{Zn} + \text{Ni}$ — the name lies: it contains $0\%$ silver.

memoryHooks: All ores are minerals; only the PROFITABLE minerals are ores.
Sulphides float, oxides leach, magnetites attract.
No air for carbonates (calcination), excess air for sulphides (roasting).
Limestone cleans the blast furnace: CaO hugs SiO₂ into slag.
Mond smells of CO (Ni); van Arkel smells of iodine (Ti, Zr).
Zone refining drags impurities down the ingot — semiconductors only.
German silver: the name lies — zero silver.
Brass has Zn, bronze has Sn — Brass-Zinc, Bronze-Tin.
Nichrome in the heater coil, duralumin in the aircraft frame.
commonMistakes: Calling every mineral an ore — profitability is the dividing line.
Using froth flotation on oxide or carbonate ores.
Swapping the calcination and roasting definitions (air is the tell).
Writing $\text{CaO}$ as the blast-furnace slag (it is the flux; slag $= \text{CaSiO}_3$).
Saying cryolite chemically reduces alumina (it is solvent/flux; reduction is electrolytic).
Assigning the Mond process to Ti (Mond = Ni; van Arkel = Ti/Zr).
Putting Sn in brass or Zn in bronze.
Listing $\text{FeS}_2$ as a workable iron ore (sulphur content is too high).
examChecklist: Match each ore formula to its metal before answering.
Pair concentration method with ore type (sulphide/oxide/magnetic).
Recite the froth-flotation roles: pine oil = collector, NaCN = depressant.
Hall–Héroult: cryolite + fluorspar lower fusion point, raise conductivity.
Refining map: Mond–Ni, van Arkel–Ti/Zr, zone–Si/Ge, electrolytic–Cu/Zn.
Alloy grid: brass, bronze, german silver, gunmetal, solder, duralumin, nichrome.
German silver contains $0\%$ Ag — say it before they ask.
Never offer $\text{FeS}_2$ as an iron ore.
